messages:
mike: Starting v2 rollout in eu-west-1 now. Canary at 5% for 30m, change window 22:00-23:00 UTC. Will ramp to 20% after smoke.

deploy-bot: deploy started: v2-api@2025-03-10T22:00Z · canary=5% · CI: https://ci.internal/build/4821 · rollout-id=rl-1755001234

kevin: Heads-up — release notes updated with breaking note about header normalization (X-Api-Version fallback behavior). Pushing to docs site, will ping client teams.

danielle: Can we pin mobile SDK traffic to v1 for the next 24h? Canary mobile errors are 1.2% vs baseline 0.3% (see short window below).

kevin: can you paste the short metric snippet?

danielle: ```
metric: requests_by_client
filter: region=eu-west-1, client=mobile
5m_error_rate: 1.2%
baseline_24h: 0.3%
``` 

mike: OK — don't want a full rollback yet. Two options: 1) pause ramp and pin mobile user-agents to v1 via routing rule, or 2) rollback header change patch. I prefer routing pin if it's quick.

jordan: Agree with routing pin. Failures skew to iOS 14 devices (old TLS stack + header parser). Pin is lower blast radius.

mike: If we pin, we'll pause ramp to 5% -> hold. I'll apply routing rule and hold traffic shift.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift: staged -> canary remains 5% · next-step paused by operator mike · rollout-id=rl-1755001234

sara: Routing rule snippet I can push to gateway:
```
route_rules:
  - match: headers.user-agent contains "MobileSDK"
    action: route_to: v1
    ttl: 24h
```

mike: Apply that and confirm. Also set rollback trigger metric: 5m error_rate > 1.5% sustained for 3 windows -> auto-rollback.

eng-oncall-bot: alert: eu-west-1 5xx spike · 5m_error_rate=1.6% · source=frontend-proxy · at=2025-03-10T22:12:05Z

jordan: That's the same window. Mobile clients account for ~70% of those 5xx in the last 5m, consistent with danielle's data.

mike: Decision: pause ramp (no further % increases), apply mobile UA pin to v1, and keep v2 canary at 5% for 60m while we monitor. No full rollback for now.

kevin: I'll send a short note to client-ops and mobile@ with a suggested client pin message and the release notes pointer.

product: Sample client-ops template (feel free to copy): "Heads up — we rolled out API v2 to eu-west-1 canary (5%). If you see elevated errors on Mobile SDK, set your app to target v1 for 24h using header X-Api-Version: 1 or upgrade SDK. Contact infra if you need a temporary route pin." :email:

danielle: Applied gateway rule and confirmed via curl from staging: `curl -H "User-Agent: MobileSDK/4.2" -I https://api.redwood.test/v2` -> responded with X-Served-Version: v1

deploy-bot: operator action recorded: route-pin applied by danielle · rollout-id=rl-1755001234

eng-oncall-bot: metrics update (22:20Z): eu-west-1 5m_error_rate dropped to 0.9% after pin · mobile-sourced errors down 60% · no new high-severity alerts

mike: Good. Keep canary at 5% and re-evaluate at 23:00 UTC. If stable, we can resume ramping but we may need a follow-up patch targeting iOS header parser.

kevin: I'll note the follow-up in the release ticket and add a client-facing blurb in release notes about the temporary pin and recommended SDK patch timeline.

sara: Also adding rollback checklist to the thread in case we need it: abort ramp, rollback to previous image v1, revoke new kernels, notify customers.

mike: Thanks all. Monitoring board is up to watch (link: https://dashboards.internal/rl-1755001234). Will update at 23:00 or earlier if anything changes. :thumbsup:
